blocks.text: 背景
多年来，TPU 一直以高性能和高效率支撑着大规模 AI 工作负载。随着智能体（agentic）和多模态工作负载的兴起，高效服务比以往任何时候都更加重要。vLLM 和 SGLang 已经通过基于 JAX 的后端在 TPU 上运行，但我们不断听到开发者表示，他们希望用 PyTorch 来自定义和调试自己的服务栈。

inlines.text: 使用 TPU Sync 迁移 KV 缓存

blocks.text: 其中两项特性让 KV cache 离开计算它的设备。分离式服务将 prefill 和 decode 运行在独立的 TPU 主机上，因此每个请求的 KV cache 都必须从 prefill 主机传输到 decode 主机。分层 KV 卸载将 HBM 中已放不下的那部分 KV cache 迁移到主机的 DRAM 以及借助 Google Cloud Managed Lustre 的二级存储，并在后续请求复用该前缀时将其取回。无论哪种方式，传输都必须与计算重叠，否则会直接增加延迟。

blocks.text: 两个引擎都为此使用 TPU Sync。它是一个用于 TPU 上 KV cache 传输与管理的开源 C++ 库。它直接读取 PyTorch 张量背后的设备缓冲区，因此传输无需在主机上额外做一次暂存拷贝，并且它在 Python 之外的独立线程上运行传输，同时 prefill 和 decode 继续进行。vLLM-TorchTPU 通过 vLLM 的 KV connector 接口将其暴露出来。SGLang-TorchTPU 将其用作分离式传输后端以及 HiCache 的 I/O 后端。

blocks.text: Background

For years, TPUs have powered large-scale AI workloads with high performance and efficiency. With the rise of agentic and multimodal workloads, serving efficiently is more important than ever. vLLM and SGLang already run on TPU through JAX-based backend, but we kept hearing from developers that they wanted to customize and debug their serving stack in PyTorch.

blocks.text: The Inference Stack

Serving at scale requires co-design across every layer of the technology stack, from silicon to compilers to orchestration. Today's launch of new inference engines is at the central part of an integrated, open TPU ecosystem.

blocks.text: Engine Overview

TorchTPU makes the TPU a native PyTorch device. Tensors are managed as standard PyTorch tensors on a tpu device with no wrapper types, code runs eagerly or compiles via torch.compile using XLA, and collectives go through torch.distributed.

Automatic prefix caching, including for hybrid models; KV cache offloading to host memory and Managed Lustre through TPU Sync; tool calling and structured output
Speculative decoding with MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark and n-gram drafters
Context parallelism for prefill and decode; FP8 KV cache; host KV offloading
Prefill and decode on separate hosts over TPU Sync, including between different parallel layouts

blocks.text: Agentic workloads in particular demand several of these features simultaneously. Because agents repeatedly resend expanding multi-turn conversations, serving them efficiently requires finding the cached prefix instead of recomputing it. Both engines keep reusable prefixes in HBM and, with host offload turned on, automatically move older prefixes to host memory as a second tier.

blocks.text: Moving the KV Cache with TPU Sync

inlines.text: Moving the KV Cache with TPU Sync

blocks.text: Two of these features move the KV cache away from the device that computed it. Disaggregated serving runs prefill and decode on separate TPU hosts, so each request's KV cache has to travel from the prefill host to the decode host.Tiered KV offload moves the part of the KV cache that no longer fits in HBM to the host's DRAM and secondary storage with Google Cloud Managed Lustre, and brings it back when a later request reuses the prefix. Either way, the transfer has to overlap computation or it adds directly to latency.

Disaggregated serving runs prefill and decode on separate TPU hosts, so each request's KV cache has to travel from the prefill host to the decode host.Tiered KV offload moves the part of the KV cache that no longer fits in HBM to the host's DRAM and secondary storage with Google Cloud Managed Lustre, and brings it back when a later request reuses the prefix. Either way, the transfer has to overlap computation or it adds directly to latency.

blocks.text: Both engines use TPU Sync for this. It is an open-source C++ library for KV cache transfer and management on TPU. It reads the device buffers behind PyTorch tensors directly, so a transfer needs no extra staging copy on the host, and it runs transfers on its own threads outside Python while prefill and decode continue. vLLM-TorchTPU exposes it through vLLM's KV connector interface. SGLang-TorchTPU uses it as a disaggregation transfer backend and as the I/O backend for HiCache.

blocks.text: Building on our initial submission of Qwen 3.5 on Ironwood TPU (TPU 7x), our engineering teams have further optimized the stack, bringing the lowest cost per million tokens overall at 2.01 cents at high-concurrency configurations. Alongside these improvements, we have also published new state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance results to AgentX, the project's dedicated track for evaluating agentic long-context and multi-turn workloads. Ironwood TPU leads across most of the Pareto frontier. We look forward to continuously updating our public performance profiles as we bring more models and configurations to the leaderboard.

blocks.text: "SGLang-TorchTPU is running in production at Meta today, and getting there was a close three-way collaboration between Meta, Google, and the SGLang team to make the stack production-ready. It gives us a remarkably mature, PyTorch-native serving stack that integrates effortlessly into our existing AI infrastructure, with the performance, reliability, and flexibility we need to run frontier workloads efficiently on TPUs. " said Zongwei Zhou, PyTorch-TPU lead at Meta.

"At RadixArk, TorchTPU has supercharged our development velocity as we roll out SGLang support across diverse silicon. It’s given us a painless path to native TPU acceleration, passing massive efficiency gains and flexible compute choices directly down to our customers," said Banghua Zhu, CTO and co-founder of RadixArk.

inlines.text: with Inferact (founded by the creators of vLLM)

blocks.text: Together, we integrated a high-performance Pallas megakernel for the 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 model that runs the entire decode step as one kernel, serving more than 700 tokens per second to a single user on Ironwood TPU. Building on this work, Inferact recently led our first preliminary AgentX submission for Kimi K3 on the vLLM-TorchTPU stack. This initial milestone already demonstrates exceptional performance per TCO in ultra-high-interactivity workloads, and the rapid increase in the maturity of the vLLM and PyTorch ecosystem on TPU for doing new frontier OSS models bring-up, with follow-up submissions set to unlock even greater efficiency through larger scale prefill/decode disaggregation.

We are thrilled to partner on the launch of TorchTPU and bring first-class support for vLLM to TPUs. By bridging PyTorch’s optimized TPU capabilities directly into vLLM, developers can immediately run production workloads on TPUs with the high throughput, low latency, and memory efficiency they expect from our stack," said Simon Mo, CEO and co-founder of Inferact.

blocks.text: Roadmap

As the models get larger, we are evolving both engines to make large-scale TPU inference deployments performant and efficient. The major features for production-grade agentic workloads are already supported. More performance optimizations and advanced features are under way – open a Github issue to request collaboration on yours!

blocks.text: Across the two engines, most of the popular open model families are supported, including Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, GPT-OSS, Gemma4 and more. The team is investing in making more models available to run natively on TPUs, including Day 0 support for new open models. We also want to give the community the tools and TPU capacity to tune performance for their own workloads and configurations.
